audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer notices that Zac's default HP-stacking build actively feeds Warwick's Jaws of the Beast (Q).
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the TARGET's maximum health and heals Warwick for damage dealt. Zac's core item is Heartsteel and his whole identity is max HP, so every point of HP Zac buys raises both Warwick's Q damage and Warwick's Q heal off him. _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this as resistances-invalidated. The answer is Grievous Wounds plus resistances rather than raw HP — the site currently recommends Heartsteel with no caveat at all.
audit.corrected: His Q scales off YOUR max health and heals him for it, so raw HP stacking feeds him — take Grievous Wounds and resistances alongside it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (Jaws of the Beast, percentHealth + heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer tells you to stay above half HP so Blood Hunt does not proc, but never says the real reason it matters at 6.
audit.why: Infinite Duress 'leaps in a direction (scaling with his bonus Move Speed)'. Blood Hunt grants Warwick move speed toward enemies below 50% health, tripled below 25%. So dropping below half HP does not merely let him chase — it physically lengthens the leap range of his 1.5s suppress. Staying above 50% is an ult-range check, which is far more actionable than a chase warning.
audit.corrected: Below 50% HP Blood Hunt speeds him up, and his R leap scales with bonus move speed — being low literally extends his suppress range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (Infinite Duress: leaps scaling with bonus Move Speed; Blood Hunt: Move Speed toward enemies below 50%)

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) is never mentioned in either layer, despite being the ability that decides whether Zac's burst lands for value.
audit.why: Primal Howl gives Warwick damage reduction for 2.5 seconds and only fears at the end of that window or on re-activation. Dumping an E-Q-W commit into a fresh Primal Howl throws the damage away, and the fear on the back end is what peels Zac off. Its cooldown is 15/14/13/12/11s, so it is up for most trades.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl is 2.5s of damage reduction first and a fear second — do not spend your combo into it, wait the 2.5s out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'level chart contradicts data: Zac wins 53.21% but the chart gives Warwick 5/7 stages vs 1.' The content chart also contradicts the full layer, which already gives Zac the First item stage.
audit.why: Warwick genuinely owns levels 1-3 on sustain and level 6 on Infinite Duress. But Levels 4-5 is where Zac's E is online and blob sustain evens the trade, and First item is where Grievous Wounds plus Heartsteel flips the grind — which is precisely the flip a 53.21% Emerald+ rate over 109 games describes. Moving those two stages produces Warwick 4 / Skill 1 / Zac 2 and reconciles the two layers.
audit.corrected: win[3] Levels 4-5 -> Skill; win[5] First item -> Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer repeats 'track Infinite Duress' throughout without ever giving a number.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70s with a 1.5s suppress; Primal Howl is 15s and Jaws of the Beast 8s at rank 1. The R number in particular reframes the lane: at rank 1 it is a 110-second cooldown, so a baited or dodged ult hands Zac an enormous window.
audit.corrected: R is 110s at rank 1 — bait or survive it once and the next two minutes are free. E is 15s, Q is 8s.

edits.before: Warwick's Jaws of the Beast (Q) heals him for a chunk of damage dealt and Blood Hunt (W) gives him movespeed to run you down when you're low — don't drop below half HP or your Unstable Matter trade just fuels his lifesteal.
edits.after: Jaws of the Beast (Q) scales off YOUR max health and heals him for it, so stacking HP feeds him — and Primal Howl (E) is 2.5s of damage reduction before the fear, so a combo dumped into it is a combo wasted.

edits.before: Infinite Duress (R) is a point-blank suppress that fully commits him; you can bait it, but if he lands it on you first he'll heal through your all-in — hold your E and R fling to answer his R, not to open.
edits.after: Infinite Duress (R) is a 1.5s suppress on a 110s rank-1 cooldown, and its leap scales with his bonus move speed — so being under 50% HP with Blood Hunt on you physically extends the range he can catch you from.

edits.after: With early bruiser/lifesteal items his Q sustain out-heals your poke — so first item is where Grievous Wounds turns the grind. Buy it before Heartsteel finishes, not after it.

notes: Chart change proposed (win[3] -> Skill, win[5] -> Zac) to clear the flagged contradiction; these are short enum-ish cells, so if the applier's +/-10% length band is applied literally to them the edit will be rejected — the band needs an exemption for chart side labels. The packet suspectName ('Let's Bounce' in spikes[3]) is a FALSE POSITIVE — the file writes "Let's Bounce!" correctly and the detector strips the '!'. I did NOT act on the _missing-interactions line 'Your Elastic Slingshot (E) shuts off Warwick's Jaws of the Beast (Q), Infinite Duress (R)' — it derives from a 'grounding' flag on Zac's E that appears to be a build-script artifact (Riot's E text says Zac 'attaches his arms to the ground'); Zac has no grounding in his kit. That bad flag will be producing false grounding claims across every Zac matchup. Not verified and left alone: whether Infinite Duress's suppression can be broken by Zac's passive revive, and whether Primal Howl's fear interrupts Let's Bounce!.
